headline: GOLD CRACKS $4,700: Metal Surges 3% on Middle East De-Escalation, Posts $1,289 Year-Over-Year Gain
snippet: Gold rose to $4,697/oz on May 6, up 3.11% from the prior session, as signs of de-escalation in the Middle East pushed oil prices lower and eased inflation concerns. The metal is up 39% year-over-year, with analysts at JP Morgan and Deutsche Bank projecting a move toward $5,000–$6,000 by year-end.

headline: BONANZA GRADE: Lundin Gold Hits 668 g/t Au Over 7.5m at Fruta del Norte — Shares Rocket 8%
snippet: Lundin Gold reported two of the highest grade-thickness holes ever drilled at Fruta del Norte, Ecuador: hole FDN-C25-374 returned 667.78 g/t Au over 7.5m and hole FDN-C26-380 returned 523.01 g/t over 8.25m — among the best results in the project's history. Shares jumped 7.9% to C$94.19, valuing the company at roughly C$23 billion.

headline: SECOND BEST EVER: Power Metallic Drills 22m at 11.46% CuEq at Lion Zone — Inaugural MRE on Track for Q3
snippet: Power Metallic Mines' hole 26-095 at the Lion Zone in Quebec returned 22m at 11.46% CuEq — the second-best intersection in the project's history — including 6.5m at 18.59% CuEq. Management says grade and thickness are being maintained and increasing as drilling advances toward an inaugural mineral resource estimate targeted for Q3 2026.

headline: SILVER RACES TO $77: Metal Outpaces Gold With 6% Daily Jump, Up 138% Year-Over-Year as Gold-Silver Ratio Hits 60
snippet: Silver surged to $77.18/oz on May 6, up 6.01% on the day and nearly double gold's 3.11% gain. Year-over-year silver is up 137.79%, compressing the gold-silver ratio to approximately 60.6. Analysts point to a structural deficit market — the sixth consecutive year of undersupply — and surging industrial demand from solar manufacturing.

headline: MAIDEN HOLES DELIVER: Collective Mining Hits 5.3m at 37 g/t Gold on Apollo's Untested Western Flank
snippet: First-ever holes targeting the western margin of Collective Mining's Apollo Ramp Zone in Colombia returned 23.15m at 4.61 g/t gold from 396m depth, including 5.3m at 37.04 g/t from 384m. With only 385m of the projected 1,500m zone circumference tested and seven rigs running, management sees major strike and depth expansion potential ahead.

headline: COPPER AT $5.70/lb: Lundin Mining Earns $380M Free Cash Flow in Q1 2026, Lifts Caserones Stake to 75%
snippet: Lundin Mining reported Q1 2026 revenue of $1.159B and $380M in free cash flow from operations, driven by 80,000 tonnes of copper production realized at $5.70/lb and gold at $5,123/oz. The company completed a $215M acquisition of an additional 5% interest in the Caserones mine in April. Full-year guidance reaffirmed.

headline: AUSTRALIA GOLD CONSOLIDATES: Regis Acquires Vault in A$10.7B All-Share Deal, Creating 700,000 oz/Year Producer
snippet: Regis Resources agreed to acquire Vault Minerals in an all-share deal valuing the combined entity at A$10.7 billion ($7.7 billion), creating Australia's third-largest primary ASX-listed gold producer with output exceeding 700,000 oz/year. Regis shareholders will own approximately 51% of the combined group; deal expected to close August–September 2026.

headline: EKATI FILES FOR SHELTER: Canada's Iconic Diamond Mine Crushed by Lab-Grown Diamonds, U.S. Tariffs, and Middle East Oil Spike
snippet: Arctic Canadian Diamond Co. (subsidiary of Burgundy Diamond Mines) filed for CCAA creditor protection on May 4, 2026, citing lab-grown diamond competition, U.S. tariffs hammering India's cutting-and-polishing industry, and Middle East-driven fuel cost increases. The company owes approximately $170M and plans to continue mining operations at Ekati during proceedings while evaluating strategic alternatives.

headline: KILOMETRE DEPTH UNLOCKED: G2 Goldfields Drills 84.5m at 3.0 g/t Au at 1km Depth — OKO Still Open Below
snippet: G2 Goldfields drilled its deepest hole to date at the OKO Project in Guyana, returning 84.5m at 3.0 g/t gold from 915m downhole — extending high-grade mineralization by 140m vertically to a depth of 1km. The zone remains open below, materially expanding the resource potential of one of Guyana's most closely watched gold projects.

headline: FINNISS BACK ONLINE: Core Lithium Begins Ore Extraction in May, Backed by $205M Including Glencore Note
snippet: Core Lithium has mobilized NRW's mining crews at the Finniss Lithium Operation near Darwin, with ore extraction from the Grants pit commencing this month after an 18-month care-and-maintenance period. The restart is funded by $205M including a $70M Glencore convertible note. Approximately 134,000t of 5% spodumene concentrate is targeted, with the first shipment planned for Q4 2026.

headline: M&A ROARS BACK: Global Mining Deals Hit $21.6B in Q1 2026 — Strongest Opening Quarter Since 2023
snippet: Global mining M&A reached $21.6B across 121 transactions in Q1 2026, the strongest first quarter since 2023 in both value and deal count. Supply-chain security for critical minerals and record gold prices are the primary drivers, with strategic partnerships increasingly structured to include private capital and government co-investment.

headline: CHINA BUYS 836 TONNES IN ONE MONTH: Silver Market Faces Sixth Straight Deficit as Solar and Investment Demand Surge
snippet: GoldSeek's weekly Gold SWOT report highlights China's March 2026 silver imports hitting an all-time monthly record of 836 tonnes, fueled by surging solar panel production and retail investment. With the global silver market projected to run a sixth consecutive structural deficit in 2026, the fundamental backdrop supports continued upward pressure on prices.

headline: NUCLEAR OR BUST: 78 Gigawatts Under Construction and AI Data Centers Need Power — Uranium Has Only One Direction
snippet: With 78 gigawatts of nuclear capacity under global construction and AI data centers creating unprecedented baseline power demand, analysts argue uranium at $86/lb is significantly underpriced relative to coming supply constraints. Utilities face record levels of uncovered uranium requirements, while new mine supply remains years from production.
